B2B services brand with limited consumer awareness, so sponsorship appetite is unclear. Details on ownership and scale are not confirmed here.

Customers are employers, mainly in retail, restaurants and logistics, and workers. Recorded funding is about 558 million dollars, probably including debt facilities. Privately held. Business-to-employer brand with moderate awareness among its worker users.

B2B health benefits brand with limited consumer awareness outside its employer customers.

B2B2C brand, known to HR teams more than consumers.

about: Purchasing Power is an Atlanta company that offers employee purchase programmes, letting workers buy products such as electronics, appliances and furniture through payroll deduction, and which has also moved into financial wellness services such as emergency savings. Its customers are employers, with employees as end users, and revenue is from product margins and fees. Crunchbase shows about $620 million in funding, with the latest round in March 2026. Privately held. Known in the HR benefits market, with limited public awareness.

about: Employment Hero is a Sydney-based cloud HR, payroll and employee benefits platform for small and medium businesses. Its products cover HR management, payroll, recruitment, employee onboarding, learning, and benefits such as the Swag discount app and earned wage access. It was founded in 2014 by Ben Thompson, serves tens of thousands of businesses in Australia, New Zealand, the UK, Singapore and Malaysia, and became a unicorn after raising more than $500M in total funding. B2B software with growing employee-facing brand awareness; it has sponsored sport in Australia.

LCI Industries is a supplier to the recreational vehicle and manufactured housing industries, headquartered in Elkhart, Indiana, listed on the NYSE (LCII). Its Lippert brand makes chassis, axles, slide-out systems, windows, doors, furniture, awnings and electronics for RV and trailer makers, with an aftermarket arm serving consumers and dealers. Major customers include Thor Industries and Forest River. Revenue is about US$3.8 billion. B2B brand with limited consumer recognition, though known in the RV community.

Alice is a Sao Paulo-based Brazilian digital healthtech company running a health plan and primary care service that combines a mobile app, a care team of doctors and nurses, and a network of partner hospitals and labs. It sells employer-paid health plans to companies and their employees, earning premiums. Founded in 2019, it is backed by Kaszek, Dragoneer and others, with Crunchbase showing about 256 million dollars raised. Growing B2B2C brand with notable awareness among Brazilian urban professionals.

about: Homebase is a San Francisco software company offering scheduling, time clock, payroll and hiring tools for hourly workers in small businesses such as restaurants and shops. Customers are small business owners in the US, paying monthly subscriptions, with tens of thousands of locations on the platform. Founded in 2014, it raised about $189 million. B2B small business software brand with little consumer awareness.

TriNet is a US professional employer organisation based in Dublin, California, providing outsourced HR services, payroll, benefits, insurance and compliance to small and mid-sized businesses, often in technology, financial services, healthcare and professional services. It serves several hundred thousand worksite employees and generates annual revenue of a few billion dollars, listed on the NYSE as TNET. Founded in 1988. B2B, with moderate brand awareness among small-business owners but none among consumers.

Wellhub, formerly Gympass, is a corporate wellness platform that gives employees of client companies access to a network of gyms, studios, fitness classes, apps and mental health and nutrition services through one monthly subscription paid by the employer or employee. It was founded in Brazil in 2012, is now headquartered in New York, and works with thousands of employers across Latin America, North America and Europe. Backed by SoftBank, General Atlantic and Valor Capital, with Crunchbase showing about 605 million dollars raised. A B2B2C brand that is well known in corporate HR circles, and increasingly to employees.

Maven Clinic is a New York digital health company, founded in 2014, offering virtual care for women's and family health, including fertility, pregnancy, postpartum, pediatrics, menopause and parenting support. Employers and health plans pay for the service as a benefit for their staff, who can access coaches and clinicians by video and chat. It serves millions of members in over a dozen countries and was valued at about 1.7 billion dollars in 2021. Backed by Oak HC/FT, General Catalyst, Sequoia and others. A B2B2C brand known among HR leaders and benefit users.

isolved is a Charlotte, North Carolina human capital management software company that provides payroll, HR, benefits, time and attendance and talent software to small and mid-sized employers, sold through its own team and partner service firms. It serves tens of thousands of client businesses and several million employees in the US. It is privately held, with Crunchbase showing a 350 million dollar financing in 2025. B2B SaaS with strong visibility among HR buyers, but low consumer awareness.

Tapcheck is a Plano, Texas fintech company, founded in 2019, offering earned wage access, which lets employees take money they have already earned before payday through a mobile app, with employers integrating the service into payroll. It makes money from fees and employer or partner arrangements, and it works with many employers, including healthcare and retail businesses. Funding shown is about 263 million dollars, mostly debt financing for advances. A B2B2C brand with limited consumer awareness.

Asure Software is an Austin-based provider of cloud human capital management software, including payroll, tax, time and attendance, HR and benefits administration for small and mid-sized businesses, sold across the US. Listed on Nasdaq (ASUR). Revenue is about 120 million dollars. Funding of 177 million dollars recorded. Customers are employers who pay subscriptions. B2B software vendor with moderate brand visibility among small businesses.

Thatch is a San Francisco-based benefits platform that offers ICHRA-style health benefits, allowing employers to give workers a tax-free allowance to choose their own insurance plan. Founded in 2021, it has raised about 192 million dollars. Customers are employers and their employees. B2B fintech and benefits brand with growing visibility among small businesses. Its customers pay monthly fees and employers fund the allowance, so brand awareness is largely driven by direct selling.

about: Flash is a Sao Paulo-based Brazilian benefits and expense platform that provides flexible benefits cards, meal and transport allowances and payments for employers. Founded in 2019, it raised about 159 million dollars, reaching unicorn status in 2022. Customers are companies and their employees. B2B fintech brand with growing consumer card use in Brazil. Its card is widely used by Brazilian workers, and revenue comes from fees, interchange and services paid by employers.

Xoxoday is a US/India software company in San Francisco offering a rewards, incentives and employee engagement platform, which lets businesses send gift cards, vouchers and experiences, and manage their marketing and HR incentives. It is part of Xoxoday's Plum, Empuls and Compass products. Funding of about 150 million dollars recorded. Customers are enterprises. B2B software with moderate awareness. Revenue comes from software subscriptions and a rewards catalogue, and customers include companies in India and the US.

about: Personio is a Munich-based human resources software company that offers an all-in-one cloud platform for small and mid-size European companies, covering recruiting, payroll, absence and employee data. Founded in 2015, it raised about $720 million and reached a valuation of $8.5 billion in 2021. Customers are SMEs across Germany, Spain, France and the UK, who pay subscriptions. It is a B2B brand well known among European HR professionals and an active marketing sponsor, though not a household name.

First Advantage is an Atlanta-area background screening and workforce identity company providing employment verification, criminal checks, drug screening and onboarding technology for employers. It is listed on Nasdaq (FA), and merged with Sterling Check in 2024. Customers are large employers across many industries. It is a B2B human resources technology brand with no consumer profile, although its name appears in job application processes.

Awardco is a Lindon, Utah employee recognition and rewards software company, with a platform for peer recognition, service awards and gifts, redeemable for items on its marketplace. Founded in 2016 and growing quickly, it raised $165 million in 2024. Customers are employers, including large companies, who pay subscriptions and fees on awards. It is a B2B human resources technology brand with no consumer profile.

US health benefits company that sells employer-based health plans, built around self-funded plans and virtual primary care, and a related testing business that rose during the COVID-19 pandemic. Curative, based in Austin, Texas, was founded by Fred Turner and ran drive-through COVID tests, then moved into insurance plans for small and mid-sized employers, with a focus on lower out-of-pocket costs for members. It raised substantial venture funding, including a large 2021 round. Customers are employers and their staff. Moderate awareness among HR buyers and COVID test users in the US.

about: Indian fintech that issues prepaid and corporate cards and runs spend-management and employee-benefit programs, including Zaggle Save, Propel rewards and loyalty, and expense and payout tools for corporates, SMEs and banks. Customers are mid-sized and large Indian companies, which use its cards for meals, fuel, gifts and incentives; it earns interchange, platform fees and voucher commissions. Founded in 2011 by Avinash Godkhindi and listed on NSE and BSE in 2022. Mostly B2B brand; end users know the card more than the company name.

Canadian junior mining company that explores and develops gold and copper properties around Merritt, British Columbia, and holds a milling facility that processes ore for itself and other miners under toll arrangements. Income is small and project-based, with value tied to precious metal prices and exploration results. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (NIM). Small resource business with low brand awareness beyond mining investors; the human resources tag is likely an input error.

PayFit is a French software company that automates payroll, HR and payslip management for small and medium businesses through a cloud platform, with features covering time-off, expenses and legal compliance. Customers are around 20,000 companies in France, the UK, Germany and Spain, who pay monthly subscriptions. Founded in 2016 in Paris, it is VC-backed (Meridiam, Accel, Eurazeo and Bpifrance) and valued above 2 billion dollars in 2021. B2B brand with significant awareness among French HR and finance teams, and it has run advertising campaigns in France.

Pebl is a US company in Palo Alto, California, described by Crunchbase as offering a global employment solution, covering hiring and employing workers across countries. It reports roughly 500 million dollars of funding, though I cannot reliably identify this specific company or its ownership. Likely a B2B HR technology and employment services business with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Kindbody is a US fertility and family-building clinic network, offering egg freezing, IVF, intrauterine insemination, fertility testing, gynaecology and employer fertility benefits, through clinics in cities such as New York, Los Angeles and Boston, plus mobile clinics. Customers are individuals and employers, and revenue comes from treatment fees and benefits contracts. Founded in 2018 by Gina Bartasi and venture backed, though it has had controversies and restructuring. Some consumer brand awareness among US women and benefits managers.

Centivo is a US digital health plan company offering self-funded employers a primary care-centred health plan, directing members to high-value providers and offering lower-cost care. Customers are mid-size employers who cover their employees' healthcare, and revenue comes from administrative and care management fees. Founded in 2016 and based in Buffalo, New York, it is venture backed. B2B healthcare brand known to benefits advisers and HR teams, with little awareness among the general public.

Topia is a US talent mobility platform that helps companies manage global employee moves, relocation, immigration, tax compliance and remote work, with software and advisory services. Customers are large employers and HR teams. Based in San Francisco, and venture and private equity backed. B2B HR technology brand known in global mobility circles, with no consumer awareness and little reason to buy F1 sponsorship, apart from hospitality for corporate clients.

about: Wrapbook is a US production payroll and cost management software company that handles payroll, benefits, insurance, tax compliance and budgeting for film, TV, commercial and live production companies, along with a production card for spending. Customers are producers and production companies in entertainment, and revenue comes from payroll fees and software. Founded in 2018 and based in New York and Los Angeles, it is venture backed. Well known in the entertainment production community, with little consumer awareness.

Indian education company based in Chennai, listed on the NSE and BSE, offering online and classroom coaching for competitive exams and professional courses. Its Veranda Race and Veranda IAS brands prepare students for banking, civil service and other government jobs, and it also teaches accounting and finance qualifications such as CA, CMA and ACCA through acquired institutes, plus skilling and school products. Customers are students and graduates paying course fees, mostly in South India. Recognisable among exam aspirants but modest overall consumer brand scale.

Youlife International is a company based in Baoshan, Shanghai, China, tagged in Crunchbase under employment and human resources. It appears in a search of listed companies, so it is publicly traded. The record gives no further detail on its services, customers or ownership, though the tags suggest staffing or HR outsourcing in China. Confirm before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Apna is a Bengaluru-based Indian professional networking and jobs app, founded in 2019 by Nirmit Parikh, aimed particularly at blue-collar, gig and early-career workers, with hundreds of communities, chat groups and job listings across cities. Users find jobs and employers advertise for roles, while Apna earns from employers, recruitment services and premium offers. It claims tens of millions of users and became a unicorn in 2021 with funding of about 193 million dollars from Tiger Global, Insight Partners and Sequoia Capital India. Strong brand recognition for jobs in Indian cities.

Chinese human-resources software company offering cloud-based talent management, recruitment, performance and payroll tools through the iTalent platform, selling subscriptions to large Chinese enterprises. about: Poland's leading online recruitment company, running Pracuj.pl and other job sites, plus HR software, serving employers and job seekers across Poland and nearby markets. Revenue comes from job advertising and subscriptions. Based in Warsaw and, after a 2024 IPO, listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. Consumer-facing brand with strong awareness in Poland.

British online pension provider that lets savers combine old workplace and personal pensions into one app-managed plan, with investment options such as Tracker, Fossil Fuel Free and Responsible Investing plans. Customers are individual UK savers, mostly digital-savvy people in their thirties to fifties, and the company earns an annual percentage fee on assets under management, with well over a billion pounds in assets and hundreds of thousands of customers. Founded in 2014 and listed on the London Stock Exchange since 2021. Strong direct-to-consumer brand with heavy TV and digital advertising and some sports sponsorship experience.

Salary Finance is a London-based financial wellbeing provider that partners with employers to offer their staff affordable loans repaid through payroll deduction, plus savings accounts and financial education tools. Employees at participating firms apply through a digital platform, the employer offers it as a benefit, and Salary Finance earns interest on the loans. Founded in 2015, it has served large UK employers including NHS trusts and major retailers, and expanded into the US. It raised significant institutional investment, including a round in 2021. Consumer awareness is mostly through employers rather than advertising.

System One is a US professional staffing and workforce solutions firm headquartered in Pittsburgh, supplying contract, direct-hire and managed-service talent in engineering, IT, scientific, clinical, finance and skilled-trades roles. Customers are large corporations in industries such as energy, life sciences, aerospace, technology and manufacturing, and revenue is the markup on placed workers' hours. It has grown through acquisitions, including Ablest and Mountain, and has revenue well above 1 billion dollars with thousands of staff. It is privately held with private equity backing. B2B brand with moderate recognition in the staffing industry and little consumer profile.

Snagajob is a US online marketplace for hourly and shift-based work, connecting job seekers with employers in restaurants, retail, hospitality, healthcare and logistics. Its website and app let workers search for, apply to and be scheduled for jobs, and employers pay for hiring, job-posting and workforce management tools. It claims over 100 million registered workers. Founded in Virginia in 2000, it is a long-running player in hourly hiring. Privately held with investors. Widely recognised by hourly workers in the US, with some consumer advertising.

Fountain is a US software company providing a hiring and onboarding platform for hourly and shift workers, used by large employers in logistics, retail, food service and healthcare. The platform automates applicant tracking, interviews, background checks and workflows, so that employers can hire at volume, and customers pay subscription fees. Founded in 2014 and based in San Francisco, it raised a Series C round in 2022. B2B software, with consumer awareness limited to job applicants and little public brand profile.

about: YuLife is a London-based insurtech that sells group life insurance, income protection and critical illness cover to employers, bundled with an app that rewards employees with points for healthy activity such as steps and meditation, redeemable for vouchers. Revenue comes from employer premiums. Founded in 2016 by Sammy Rubin, it expanded to the US and South Africa and built a customer base of thousands of employers and hundreds of thousands of insured staff. It raised significant venture funding. Known to employers and employees more than to the general public.

Karat is a US company that provides technical interviewing as a service: its trained engineers, called Interview Engineers, run structured coding and system-design interviews on behalf of employers, returning scored evidence to recruiters and hiring managers, and it offers an interview platform and a talent marketplace. Customers include large technology companies, banks and consumer firms. Revenue comes from per-interview fees and subscriptions. Founded in 2014 and based in Seattle, it has conducted hundreds of thousands of interviews. B2B product, known in engineering hiring circles but not to the general public.

Minneapolis health insurer that designs insurance plans for self-funded employers, offering transparent pricing and fixed costs and an on-demand approach where members know prices before treatment. Customers are employers and their employees. Founded in 2016 and venture-funded, with investors in healthcare. B2B2C, with low visibility among consumers. Bind sells through brokers and employer groups, and its plans are fully insured rather than administered by a traditional carrier.
